goal: Hides CTransaction's data members behind const observer functions instead of leaving them public and const.
Author frames this as removing 'class layout as API' coupling, enabling future work like a serialization boundary, an immutable shared body, or arena-based transaction storage.
Adds a reusable clang-tidy check (use-observers) to automate the mechanical migration.

l0rinc gave an Approach NACK, offering an alternative smaller-step branch and objecting to the new Get* naming and CMutableTransaction duplication (l0rinc).
Several members gave Concept ACKs finding the encapsulation valuable in itself and as groundwork for future work (josibake, w0xlt, janb84, willcl-ark, ryanofsky).

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because it changes the core CTransaction primitive's representation, and resolving the underlying disagreement is a precondition for further encapsulation work (COutPoint, CBlock, per #35904) and for a possible future arena-based transaction layout sipa flagged as newly relevant given #36015.
The change itself is behavior-preserving today (no consensus, correctness, or performance delta demonstrated), so the payoff is speculative rather than realized.

result.summary: This PR encapsulates CTransaction's data members (vin, vout, version, nLockTime) behind public const observer functions, then makes the members private and non-const, migrating all ~90 call sites mechanically via a new bitcoin-tidy check (use-observers). The change is deliberately split into three commits (add observers, mechanically migrate call sites, make members private) so reviewers can separate handwritten from automated changes and so rebases can reset and rerun the tool on conflicting files. It is presented as groundwork for later refactors (serialization decoupling, a possibly regular/immutable value type, arena-based storage) described in the author's blog posts and issue #35904, but does not itself change CTransaction's runtime behavior.
result.problem: CTransaction currently exposes its representation (public const data members) as its API, which the author argues tightly couples ~90 call sites to the concrete layout and blocks future changes to how transactions are stored or constructed (e.g. a shared immutable body, an arena allocator, or decoupled (de)serialization). Whether this coupling is currently causing real harm, versus being a speculative future concern, is exactly what much of the discussion disputes.

open_concerns: ajtowns: Concept NACK — believes the abstraction buys nothing today, calls it a waste of scarce review resources on consensus-critical code, and is skeptical the described serialization/perf follow-ups actually require this change.

l0rinc: Approach NACK — objects to the scale of the mechanical diff, the new Get*() naming versus keeping protocol vocabulary (vin/vout), and CMutableTransaction gaining duplicate observers; proposed an alternative smaller-step branch.

mzumsande: skeptical that generic C++ guideline arguments alone justify touching core consensus code without a concrete Bitcoin-Core-specific payoff; also flagged that generic accessor naming diverges from protocol terminology used at the RPC layer.
Extended meta-discussion about tone/conduct occurred and was redirected by a maintainer to the meta repo, without resolving the substantive technical disagreement.
resolved_concerns: janb84's find of an unmigrated GetValueOut() template instantiation was fixed in a follow-up push.
josibake's concern about move-constructor safety was addressed by not providing a move constructor for CTransaction.
maflcko's nits on [[nodiscard]] and std:: prefix were addressed (removed) by the author.

l0rinc's naming-conflict question (why not name accessors vin()/vout()) was answered: C++ disallows a member function and data member sharing a name, which would break the three-step migration; author documented this and other resolutions in a summary comment on 2026-08-24.
alexanderwiederin verified the mechanical fixup commit is byte-reproducible and that tests pass, giving an ACK.
discussion.author_status: active, most recently pushing 2026-08-24 and posting a comprehensive summary of resolved questions; author has been engaging continuously with reviewers throughout the thread

How much weight to give speculative future benefits (arena allocation, serialization decoupling) that are not implemented in this PR, versus the concrete claim that it is purely mechanical churn.
result.card: This PR encapsulates CTransaction by moving its public const data members (vin, vout, version, nLockTime) behind const observer functions, then making them private, migrating ~90 call sites via a new self-written clang-tidy check. It is presented as groundwork for future work (a possible immutable value type, arena-based storage, decoupled serialization) rather than a behavior change itself, and is labeled Validation. The PR triggered an unusually long and contentious debate: ajtowns issued a Concept NACK calling it a waste of review resources on consensus code, l0rinc gave an Approach NACK proposing an alternative smaller-step branch, while josibake, ryanofsky, w0xlt, janb84, and willcl-ark gave Concept ACKs, and alexanderwiederin gave a verified ACK after independently reproducing the mechanical fixup byte-for-byte with green tests. sipa flagged a concrete potential future payoff (arena allocation for transaction storage, newly relevant to #36015) that this PR does not itself implement. The code is reviewable now (CI green, reproducible, no rebase needed) even though the underlying concept/approach dispute remains unresolved despite extensive author engagement.
